Title: AKU Medical College, Pakistan launches strategic planning exercise
NewsSummary: Working groups will deliberate and make recommendations to strengthen academic culture and performance.
NewsContent:
In order to meet and capitalize on emerging challenges and opportunities, remain contextually relevant and consolidate on existing strengths to allow for its continued excellence, the Medical College, Pakistan initiated a major strategic planning and strengthening exercise to deliberate and make recommendations with reference to the mission, vision and mandate of the Medical College, Pakistan and the Aga Khan University (AKU). 

"A university's role ultimately is to educate, to produce new knowledge, to help understand the issues that society is facing and to then impart that knowledge in a way that improves the quality of life for an individual and society. At AKU, we do that through our research, knowledge, education and service", said Mr Firoz Rasul, President and Interim Provost, AKU, in his introductory remarks at the official launch of the exercise, on Thursday at the AKU Auditorium.

The Interim Provost also emphasised the need to reflect on several trends that are redefining the global education and health landscape, including:

The changing role of the 'educator' in teaching and education, owing to the use of and advancements in technology, varying education systems and the evolving nature of students: educators are no longer seen just as teachers or 'imparters of knowledge' but as coaches, facilitators and mentors, which significantly affects how learners in formal and informal learning spaces are engaged.

The significance of multi-disciplinarity and its value and impact on student learning

Rapid advancements in technology and their impact on the way medicine and nursing are practiced and taught

The gradual shift from health-care being provided solely in hospitals, due to increasing costs, lack of access, technology advancements and changing lifestyles

The recent explosion of Massive Open Online Courses by leading global universities and the general population's reluctance to complete the courses after starting them despite their access to all relevant learning resources

The ability to attain a balance between what is relevant and appropriate to the local context yet competitive in global markets

To ensure meaningful and focused discussions, Working Groups have been constituted to deliberate on the progress, developments, innovations, issues and challenges in key areas including: Undergraduate programmes, Graduate programmes, Postgraduate programmes, Continuing Professional Education/Continuing Medical Education programmes, Research and Faculty matters (including faculty campus life, faculty development, succession planning, leadership development, academic support structures and academic/service balance, amongst many others).

The groups will conduct a self-analysis in each area over a six-week period and will present their findings and recommendations at two half-day workshops: one on teaching/learning and associated activities; and the other on research, scholarship and faculty matters, planned for April/May 2016. The recommendations of the groups will become part of a wider Medical College, Pakistan strategic plan as it enters into its next phase of development.
